blocks.content: 1. MEANING OF NATIONAL INCOME

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: National Income is the total net monetary value of all final goods and services produced by normal residents of a country in a financial year.
Market Price is derived by adding Net Indirect Taxes (Indirect Taxes minus Subsidies) to Factor Cost.
Gross Value Added (GVA) gives sector-wise (Primary, Secondary, Tertiary) estimates of economic output.
Real GDP is measured at constant base year prices (2011-12) to reflect actual volume growth without inflation distortion.
Transfer payments, capital gains, windfall gains, and second-hand goods sales are excluded from National Income accounting.

blocks.content: National Income refers to the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country during a financial year.
In India, financial year runs from 1 April to 31 March.
2. CORE NATIONAL INCOME CONCEPTS

cells: Value of final goods & services within domestic territory
NNP at Market Price – Indirect Taxes + Subsidies

blocks.content: 3. METHODS OF MEASURING NATIONAL INCOME

1. Production Method (Value Added Method): Sum of value added at each stage of production.

2. Income Method: Sum of factor incomes (Wages + Rent + Interest + Profit).

3. Expenditure Method: C + I + G + (X – M).
4. GROSS VALUE ADDED (GVA)
GVA measures the value of goods and services produced in a sector after deducting intermediate consumption.
Formula: GVA = Output – Intermediate Consumption.
National Income measures the total net money value of all final goods and services produced by normal residents of a country during a financial year.
India shifted focus to GVA in 2015 for better sectoral analysis.
5. FACTOR COST vs MARKET PRICE
6. BASE YEAR IN NATIONAL INCOME
Base year is the reference year used for comparison of economic data.
India's current GDP base year is 2011–12.

rows: Valued at current year market prices
Valued at constant base year prices
Includes the impact of price inflation
Adjusted to remove the effect of inflation
Can rise due to inflation alone without real output growth
Reflects genuine physical output changes in the economy

blocks.content: Base year is revised periodically to reflect structural changes in the economy.
7. CSO & NATIONAL ACCOUNTS
Earlier, National Income was estimated by Central Statistical Organisation (CSO).
Now it is prepared by National Statistical Office (NSO) under Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
8. PURCHASING POWER PARITY (PPP)
PPP is an economic theory used to compare economic productivity and living standards between countries.
It adjusts exchange rates according to price level differences.
India is among the top economies in the world in terms of PPP.

items: Factor Cost vs Market Price: Market Price = Factor Cost + Indirect Taxes - Subsidies.
Exclusions from National Income: Transfer payments (like pensions, scholarships) and illegal income are strictly excluded.
Base Year Concept: India currently uses 2011-12 as the base year for calculating real GDP and national accounts estimates.

10. ITEMS NOT INCLUDED IN NATIONAL INCOME

• Transfer payments (pension, scholarships)

• Sale of second-hand goods

• Illegal activities

• Intermediate goods (to avoid double counting)
11. RRB ULTRA IMPORTANT ONE-LINERS

• GNP = GDP + NFIA

• NNP at FC = NNP at MP – Indirect Tax + Subsidy

• Base Year (India) – 2011–12

• National Income estimated by NSO

• GVA = Output – Intermediate Consumption

• GDP Deflator measures inflation
